text: The number of turns of the coil of a moving coil galvanometer is increased in order to increase current sensitivity by $50%$. The percentage change in voltage sensitivity of the galvanometer will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a moving coil galvanometer, the current sensitivity is $S_{I}=\dfrac{θ}{I}=\dfrac{NAB}{k}$ and the voltage sensitivity is $S_{V}=\dfrac{θ}{V}=\dfrac{θ}{IR}=\dfrac{NAB}{kR}$.

$S_{I}\propto N$, so a $50%$ rise in current sensitivity needs $N^{'}=1.5N$.

The coil is wound from the same wire, so its length, and hence its resistance, grows in proportion to the number of turns: $R^{'}=1.5R$.

$S_{V}^{'}=\dfrac{1.5NAB}{k(1.5R)}=\dfrac{NAB}{kR}=S_{V}$

The voltage sensitivity is unchanged, a change of $0%$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: A body weight $\mathrm{W}$, is projected vertically upwards from earth's surface to reach a height above the earth which is equal to nine times the radius of earth. The weight of the body at that height will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The weight of an object varies with altitude due to the change in gravitational force. The force of gravity decreases with the square of the distance from the center of the Earth.

The gravitational force (weight) at a height h from the surface of the Earth is given by:

$W^{'}=W\left (\frac{R}{R+h}\right )^{2}$

where:

W' is the weight at height h,
W is the weight at the Earth's surface,
R is the radius of the Earth,
h is the height above the Earth's surface.

In this problem, the height h is given as nine times the radius of the Earth (h = 9R). Substituting h = 9R into the equation gives:

$W^{'}=W\left (\frac{R}{R+9R}\right )^{2}=W\left (\frac{1}{10}\right )^{2}$

Simplifying this gives:

$W^{'}=\frac{W}{100}$

Therefore, the weight of the body at that height will be 1/100th of its weight on the surface of the Earth. 

The correct answer is Option C: $\frac{W}{100}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: Considering a group of positive charges, which of the following statements is correct ?
options: Net potential of the system cannot be zero at a point but net electric field can be zero at that point
Net potential of the system at a point can be zero but net electric field can't be zero at that point.
Both the net potential and the net electric field cannot be zero at a point.
Both the net potential and the net field can be zero at a point.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The net potential is the scalar sum $V=\sum \dfrac{kq_{i}}{r_{i}}$. Every $q_{i}$ is positive and every $r_{i}$ is positive and finite, so every term is positive and $V>0$ at every point; the net potential cannot be zero.

The net field is the vector sum of the individual fields, which can cancel. At the midpoint of two equal positive charges $q$ a distance $d$ apart, the two fields are equal and opposite, so $E=0$, while $V=\dfrac{4kq}{d}\neq 0$.

So the field can be zero at a point but the potential cannot, which rules out (B), (C) and (D); the point at infinity, where $V=0$ only because it is chosen as the reference, is not a point at a finite distance from the charges.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: A long conducting wire having a current I flowing through it, is bent into a circular coil of $\mathrm{N}$ turns. Then it is bent into a circular coil of $\mathrm{n}$ turns. The magnetic field is calculated at the centre of coils in both the cases. The ratio of the magnetic field in first case to that of second case is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The same wire of length $L$ forms $N$ turns of radius $r_{1}$, so $L=N(2πr_{1})$ and $r_{1}=\dfrac{L}{2πN}$.

The field at the centre of $N$ turns is

$B_{1}=\frac{μ_{0}NI}{2r_{1}}=\frac{μ_{0}NI}{2}\times \frac{2πN}{L}=\frac{πμ_{0}IN^{2}}{L}$

With $n$ turns, $r_{2}=\dfrac{L}{2πn}$ and in the same way $B_{2}=\dfrac{πμ_{0}In^{2}}{L}$.

$\frac{B_{1}}{B_{2}}=\frac{N^{2}}{n^{2}}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
A water heater of power $2000\mathrm{W}$ is used to heat water. The specific heat capacity of water is $4200\mathrm{J}$ $\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\mathrm{K}^{-1}$. The efficiency of heater is $70%$. Time required to heat $2\mathrm{kg}$ of water from $10^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ to $60^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ is $_________ s$.

 (Assume that the specific heat capacity of water remains constant over the temperature range of the water).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of a substance can be calculated as:

Q = m $\times$ c $\times$ ΔT

where Q is the heat energy required, m is the mass of the substance, c is its specific heat capacity, and ΔT is the change in temperature.

The time required to heat a substance can be calculated as :

t = $\frac{Q}{P}$

where t is the time required, and P is the power of the heating device.

The actual power output of the heating device can be calculated as:

$P_{$actual$} = P_{$input} $\times$ efficiency

where $P_$input is the input power to the device and efficiency is the fraction of input power that is actually converted to useful power output.

Substituting the given values:

Q = 2 kg $\times$ 4200 J/kg/K $\times$ (60 - 10) = 2 kg $\times$ 4200 J/kg/K $\times$ 50 K = 4200 $\times$ 50 $\times$ 2 J = 420,000 J

$P_{$input} = 2000 W = 2000 J/s

$P_{$actual} = 2000 $\times$ 0.7 = 1400 J/s

t = $\frac{Q}{P_{actual}}$ = $\frac{420,000}{1400}$ J/s = 300 s

So, the time required to heat 2 kg of water from 10°C to 60°C is approximately 300 s.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: Two bodies are projected from ground with same speeds $40\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ at two different angles with respect to horizontal. The bodies were found to have same range. If one of the body was projected at an angle of $60^{\circ }$, with horizontal then sum of the maximum heights, attained by the two projectiles, is $________$ $\mathrm{m}$. (Given $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{ms}^{-2}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When two bodies are projected from the ground at the same speed of $40\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ but at different angles, and they achieve the same range, we can derive the following:

Given that one projectile is launched at an angle of $60^{\circ }$ with respect to the horizontal, let's denote the angles of projection as $θ_{1}$ and $θ_{2}$. For the ranges to be equal, we know:

$θ_{1}+θ_{2}=90^{\circ }$

Since $θ_{1}=60^{\circ }$, we can find $θ_{2}$ as:

$θ_{2}=30^{\circ }$

Next, to find the sum of the maximum heights attained by both projectiles, we use the formula for the maximum height $H_{\max }$:

$H_{\max }=\frac{u^{2}\sin ^{2}θ}{2g}$

For the first body projected at $60^{\circ }$:

$(H_{\max })_{1}=\frac{(40)^{2}\sin ^{2}60^{\circ }}{2\times 10}$

Since $\sin 60^{\circ }=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$:

$(H_{\max })_{1}=\frac{1600\times \left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )^{2}}{20}=\frac{1600\times \frac{3}{4}}{20}=\frac{1200}{20}=60\mathrm{m}$

For the second body projected at $30^{\circ }$:

$(H_{\max })_{2}=\frac{(40)^{2}\sin ^{2}30^{\circ }}{2\times 10}$

Since $\sin 30^{\circ }=\frac{1}{2}$:

$(H_{\max })_{2}=\frac{1600\times \left (\frac{1}{2}\right )^{2}}{20}=\frac{1600\times \frac{1}{4}}{20}=\frac{400}{20}=20\mathrm{m}$

Therefore, the sum of the maximum heights attained by both projectiles is:

$(H_{\max })_{1}+(H_{\max })_{2}=60\mathrm{m}+20\mathrm{m}=80\mathrm{m}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

solution.body:
$\mathrm{E}_{H}=13.6$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Li}^{2+}}=13.6\dfrac{Z^{2}}{n^{2}}=13.6\times \dfrac{9}{9}=13.6\mathrm{eV} \\  \\ =136\times 10^{-1}\mathrm{eV} \end{array}$

text:
Two parallel plate capacitors $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ each having capacitance of $10μ\mathrm{F}$ are individually charged by a 100 V D.C. source. Capacitor $C_{1}$ is kept connected to the source and a dielectric slab is inserted between its plates. Capacitor $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ is disconnected from the source and then a dielectric slab is inserted in it. Afterwards the capacitor $C_{1}$ is also disconnected from the source and the two capacitors are finally connected in parallel combination. The common potential of the combination will be $________ V$.

(Assuming Dielectric constant $=10$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With the source connected, the potential of $C_{1}$ stays $V=100\text{V}$ while its capacitance becomes $KC=10\times 10μ\text{F}=100μ\text{F}$, so its charge is

$Q_{1}=KCV=100μ\text{F}\times 100\text{V}=10000μ\text{C}$

$C_{2}$ is disconnected before the slab is inserted, so its charge stays at its original value while its capacitance also becomes $KC=100μ\text{F}$:

$Q_{2}=CV=10μ\text{F}\times 100\text{V}=1000μ\text{C}$

On joining them in parallel, the total charge is conserved and both capacitors reach one common potential:

$V_{\text{common}}=\dfrac{Q_{1}+Q_{2}}{KC+KC}=\dfrac{10000+1000}{100+100}\text{V}=55\text{V}$

Since the two capacitances are equal, each capacitor finally carries half the total charge, $5500μ\text{C}$, which again gives $5500μ\text{C}/100μ\text{F}=55\text{V}$.

Hence, the answer is 55.
